src.q: Mebeverine hydrochloride 200 mg. Excipient with known effect

bnf.note: BNF/BNFC is only available in the UK; not accessed.

items.t: Symptomatic relief of irritable bowel syndrome.

src.q: For the symptomatic relief of irritable bowel syndrome.

restrictions.note: No prescribing restriction stated in the UK SmPC accessed (UK 200 mg modified-release capsule SmPC).

items.t: Adults: 200 mg (one capsule) twice daily, one in the morning and one in the evening. Duration of use is not limited.

src.q: One capsule of 200 mg twice daily, to be given one in the morning and one in the evening.
Duration of use is not limited.

items.t: Elderly, renal or hepatic impairment: no dose adjustment considered necessary (no dedicated studies).

src.q: No dosage adjustment is deemed necessary in elderly, renal and/or hepatic impaired patients.

items.t: Not recommended under 18 years (insufficient safety and efficacy data).

src.q: not recommended for use in children and adolescents below 18, due to insufficient data on safety and efficacy

items.t: Hypersensitivity to mebeverine or any excipient.

src.q: Hypersensitivity to the active substance or to any of the excipients listed in section 6.1.

items.t: Contains sucrose: patients with hereditary fructose intolerance, glucose-galactose malabsorption or sucrase-isomaltase insufficiency should not take it.

src.q: Patients with rare hereditary problems of fructose intolerance, glucose-galactose malabsorption or sucrose-isomaltese insufficiency should not take this medicine.

items.t: No interaction studies except with alcohol; animal studies showed no interaction with ethanol.

src.q: No interaction studies have been performed, except with alcohol.
demonstrated the absence of any interaction between mebeverine hydrochloride and ethanol

items.t: No dose adjustment considered necessary in renal impairment (no posology studies; no specific risk seen post-marketing).

src.q: No posology studies in elderly, renal and/or hepatic impaired patients have been performed.
No dosage adjustment is deemed necessary in elderly, renal and/or hepatic impaired patients.

items.t: No dose adjustment considered necessary in hepatic impairment (no posology studies; no specific risk seen post-marketing).

src.q: No posology studies in elderly, renal and/or hepatic impaired patients have been performed.
No dosage adjustment is deemed necessary in elderly, renal and/or hepatic impaired patients.

items.t: SmPC: no or limited human data; not recommended in pregnancy.

src.q: There are no or limited amounts of data from the use of mebeverine in pregnant women.
Mebeverine is not recommended during pregnancy.

items.t: BUMPS: antispasmodics are occasionally used in pregnancy when needed to control IBS or diverticular disease; very little information, so safety for the baby is unclear.

src.q: Antispasmodics are occasionally used in pregnancy if they are needed to control diverticular disease or IBS.
There is very little information on women taking antispasmodics in pregnancy so it unclear if they are safe for the baby.

items.t: SmPC: not known if it passes into milk; should not be used during breastfeeding.

src.q: It is unknown whether mebeverine or its metabolites are excreted in human milk.
Mebeverine should not be used during breast-feeding.

items.t: SPS: can be used with caution; low milk levels expected; monitor the infant for allergic reactions or unusual behaviour.

src.q: Mebeverine can be used during breastfeeding, but infant monitoring is required.
monitor infants for allergic reactions or any other signs of unusual behaviour

items.t: No clinical fertility data; animal studies show no harmful effect.

src.q: There are no clinical data on male or female fertility; however, animal studies do not indicate harmful effects of mebeverine

adverseCommon.note: The UK 200 mg modified-release capsule SmPC lists only post-marketing reactions with no frequency (see serious adverse effects).

items.t: Hypersensitivity including anaphylactic reactions; urticaria, angioedema, face oedema, exanthema (frequency not known).

src.q: Hypersensitivity (anaphylactic reactions)
Urticaria, angioedema, face oedema, exanthema.

monitoring.note: No monitoring requirements stated in the UK SmPC accessed (UK 200 mg modified-release capsule SmPC); no SPS monitoring page found.

items.t: Swallow capsules with plenty of water (at least 100 mL); do not chew (modified-release coating).

src.q: The capsules should be swallowed with a sufficient amount of water (at least 100 ml water). They should not be chewed because the coating is intended to ensure a prolonged release mechanism

items.t: Missed dose: carry on with the next dose; do not take extra to make up.

src.q: the missed dose(s) should not be taken in addition to the regular dose

items.t: Not expected to affect driving or using machines.

src.q: do not indicate any harmful effect of mebeverine on the ability to drive or to use machines

rules.sourceWording: 4.3 Contraindications: Hypersensitivity to the active substance

src.q: Hypersensitivity to the active substance or to any of the excipients listed in section 6.1.

rules.concern: Hereditary fructose intolerance, glucose-galactose malabsorption or sucrase-isomaltase insufficiency (contains sucrose)

src.q: Patients with rare hereditary problems of fructose intolerance, glucose-galactose malabsorption or sucrose-isomaltese insufficiency should not take this medicine.

rules.sourceWording: not recommended for use in children and adolescents below 18

src.q: not recommended for use in children and adolescents below 18, due to insufficient data on safety and efficacy
Mebeverine is not recommended during pregnancy.

rules.consequence: Very little information; unclear if safe for the baby. Antispasmodics are occasionally used in pregnancy when needed for IBS or diverticular disease.
rules.sourceWording: occasionally used in pregnancy if they are needed

src.q: Antispasmodics are occasionally used in pregnancy if they are needed to control diverticular disease or IBS.
There is very little information on women taking antispasmodics in pregnancy so it unclear if they are safe for the baby.

rules.consequence: Not known if it passes into milk.
rules.action: Should not be used during breastfeeding.
rules.sourceWording: should not be used during breast-feeding

src.q: Mebeverine should not be used during breast-feeding.

rules.consequence: Low milk levels expected, but properties less favourable than other antispasmodics.
rules.action: Can be used with infant monitoring (allergic reactions, unusual behaviour).

src.q: Mebeverine can be used during breastfeeding, but infant monitoring is required.
monitor infants for allergic reactions or any other signs of unusual behaviour
